html:
The Uyghur Khaganate was a Turkic empire on the Mongolian steppe from 744 to 840. The Uyghurs overthrew the second Türk Khaganate and took over its lands.

The Uyghurs were close allies of Tang China. When the An Lushan Rebellion nearly destroyed the Tang, Uyghur cavalry helped retake the capitals Chang'an and Luoyang in 757. In return the Tang paid them in silk, mostly in exchange for horses, a trade that made the khagans rich.

They did something unusual for steppe rulers: they built cities. Their capital Ordu-Baliq in the Orkhon valley had walls, a palace and markets. Sogdian merchants and advisers were influential at court, and in 763 the khagan adopted Manichaeism, a Persian religion, as the faith of the state. It is the only state that ever did so.

In 840 the Yenisei Kyrgyz from the north sacked Ordu-Baliq and the empire collapsed. The Uyghurs scattered south:

  • to Gansu, where they founded the Ganzhou kingdom
  • to the Turfan oases, where they founded the kingdom of Qocho, which became largely Buddhist

The Uyghur script they used later became the script for writing Mongolian. The modern Uyghurs of Xinjiang take their name from this people, part of the larger Turkic migrations.
sum: The Uyghur Khaganate was a Turkic empire on the Mongolian steppe from 744 to 840. The Uyghurs overthrew the second Türk Khaganate and took over its lands.
